sx.note: Hidden vitality S tracks observed fitness X very strongly, so balancing X also balances S (the Wasserstein lever).

prop.note: Moderate selection on the hidden vitality (e=σ(0.8S−2X)): enough to confound, small enough to keep the matched Γ small.

outcome.note: Blue=treated, red=control. Square=S=+1, circle=S=−1, bold=avg over S. Vitality shifts BOTH arms by ~8 (huge model bias); therapy adds 1.0S+1.5X.

cate.note: The true effect crosses zero at X=0: treat the fit (X>0), spare the unfit (X<0). Subtle vs the ~8-unit confounding bias.

obs.note: Observed covariate imbalance between arms (the residual the Wasserstein term corrects).

val_uncap_ce1.note: UNCAPPED, c_ε=1: realised E[Y] vs Γ (N=600, 5-seed mean). O-W (circles) peak at Γ=2–3 above every other method; the regret method Hajek-O-X collapses to never-treat; IPW-O-W softens past Γ≈4 (more so at larger c_ε). X-X (dashed) is Γ-free.
